verses.2: I know that this is true: How can a human be just before God?
verses.3: If He wishes to contend with Him, He will not answer Him even one of a thousand.
verses.4: Wise in heart and mighty in strength—who is so bold as to challenge Him and remain unscathed?
verses.5: The One who removes mountains and they do not know it, who overturns them in His anger.
verses.6: The One who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble.
verses.7: The One who says to the sun, “Do not shine,” and seals the stars.
verses.8: The One who spreads the heavens alone and treads the vaults of the sea.
verses.9: The One who makes the Pleiades, Orion, and the constellations of the south.
verses.10: The One who does great things beyond reckoning, and wonders beyond numbering.
verses.11: Look, He passes over me, and I do not see Him; He moves past, and I do not understand.
verses.12: Look, He seizes me—who can stop Him? Who can say to Him, “What are You doing?”
verses.13: God does not turn back His anger; beneath Him are the helpers of Rahab crouched.
verses.14: Even if I were to speak with Him, I would not be heard; I would not be answered, even if I had to argue my case.
verses.15: If I am righteous, He will not listen to me; He will not grant me justice in His judgment.
verses.16: If I called, and He answered, I would not believe that He had heard my voice.
verses.17: He storms over me in the whirlwind and multiplies my wounds without cause.
verses.18: He does not allow my spirit to breathe; He fills me with bitterness.
verses.19: If He is strong, who can oppose Him? If He judges, who will argue with Him?
verses.20: If I am innocent, my mouth will condemn me; if I am clean, He will find me guilty.
verses.21: I am innocent, but I do not know myself; I despise my life.
verses.22: One thing I know, and that is what I have said: The righteous and the wicked He both destroy.
verses.23: If the rod kills suddenly, the innocent are mocked in death.
verses.24: The land is given into the hands of the wicked; the faces of its judges are covered. If it is not Him, who is it?
verses.25: My days are lighter than a runner; they have fled and seen no good.
verses.26: They have passed like the path of a ship, like an eagle that flies to seek food.
verses.27: If I say, “I will forget my complaint, I will remove my face and be cheerful,”
verses.28: I am in fear of all my bones, for I know that You will not acquit me.
verses.29: If I am guilty, why should I strive in vain?
verses.30: If I were to wash myself in fresh snow and my hands would become pure,
verses.31: still, You would plunge me into the mud, and my garments would despise me.
verses.32: For He is not a man like me, that I could answer Him and confront Him in court.
verses.33: There is no arbiter between us who might place his hand over us both.
verses.34: Remove Your rod from me, and let Your fear not terrify me.
verses.35: I would speak and not fear You, for I am not like You.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 13: “the helpers of Rahab crouched” — Rahab here is a poetic metaphor for chaos or the sea.  
- v. 31: “the mud” — the Hebrew term is *shachat*, which is often rendered as “mire” or “slime.”  
- v. 33: “no arbiter between us” — the Hebrew word *mocheach* is used in the sense of an arbiter or mediator.
